contents.text: Look back at the passage. These choices are correct:

content.text: We should focus on wool production, since our pastureland is good for sheep.

explanationText.text: Adam Smith says that the industry, or economic activity, of a country should "find out the way in which it can be employed to the greatest advantage." So, Smith would likely agree that if a country has an advantage of good pastureland for sheep, then they should focus on wool production.

content.text: Since our climate is cold, we should trade with a warmer country to get tropical fruit.

explanationText.text: Adam Smith says that a country should "never attempt to make at home what it will cost him more to make than to buy." Tropical fruit is easier and cheaper to grow in a warm climate, so Smith would likely agree that a colder country should trade to get fruit.

contents.text: These choices are not correct:

content.text: A neighboring country produces a lot more wheat than we do, so we should invest in our wheat industry.

explanationText.text: Adam Smith says that a country should "never attempt to make at home what it will cost him more to make than to buy." A country that is already specialized in wheat production can provide lower costs for consumers. So, Smith would likely disagree that a country should try to start growing its own wheat.

content.text: Our dairy industry is struggling, so we should focus government resources on strengthening it.

explanationText.text: Adam Smith says that a country should "find out the way in which it can be employed to the greatest advantage" and trade for the rest. So, Smith would likely disagree that a country should spend its resources on a struggling industry.

textContent.text: Economists use the term aggregate demand, often shortened to demand, to describe the total amount of money spent on goods and services. It includes money spent by households, companies, and the government. An increase in demand is associated with economic growth.

When people spend more money on goods and services, the prices of those goods and services typically increase. The rate at which prices generally rise is called inflation. Inflation can also happen when goods and services become harder to acquire. This is usually due to an increase in production costs or a reduction in the supply of goods.

Alongside demand and inflation, another indicator called unemployment is the percentage of people in an economy who are able to work but cannot find a job. Unemployment is usually low when demand is high because more workers are needed to provide the goods and services that people spend money on.

Most U.S. policymakers think a healthy economy features high demand, low unemployment, and stable, moderate inflation. When demand decreases and unemployment rises, economies enter periods called recessions. Recessions are examples of an unhealthy economy, and policymakers usually try to prevent them.

textContent.text: Economists use the term aggregate demand, often shortened to demand, to describe the total amount of money spent on goods and services. It includes money spent by households, companies, and the government. An increase in demand is associated with economic growth.

When people spend more money on goods and services, the prices of those goods and services typically increase. The rate at which prices generally rise is called inflation. Inflation can also happen when goods and services become harder to acquire. This is usually due to an increase in production costs or a reduction in the supply of goods.

Alongside demand and inflation, another indicator called unemployment is the percentage of people in an economy who are able to work but cannot find a job. Unemployment is usually low when demand is high because more workers are needed to provide the goods and services that people spend money on.

Most U.S. policymakers think a healthy economy features high demand, low unemployment, and stable, moderate inflation. When demand decreases and unemployment rises, economies enter periods called recessions. Recessions are examples of an unhealthy economy, and policymakers usually try to prevent them.

textContent.text: Economists use the term aggregate demand, often shortened to demand, to describe the total amount of money spent on goods and services. It includes money spent by households, companies, and the government. An increase in demand is associated with economic growth.

When people spend more money on goods and services, the prices of those goods and services typically increase. The rate at which prices generally rise is called inflation. Inflation can also happen when goods and services become harder to acquire. This is usually due to an increase in production costs or a reduction in the supply of goods.

Alongside demand and inflation, another indicator called unemployment is the percentage of people in an economy who are able to work but cannot find a job. Unemployment is usually low when demand is high because more workers are needed to provide the goods and services that people spend money on.

Most U.S. policymakers think a healthy economy features high demand, low unemployment, and stable, moderate inflation. When demand decreases and unemployment rises, economies enter periods called recessions. Recessions are examples of an unhealthy economy, and policymakers usually try to prevent them.
